title: Romaji And Kana Input Check
concept: Japanese spelling, pronunciation, and IME input

questions.prompt: Which learner-facing romaji correctly shows how こんばんは is pronounced?
questions.explanation: The final は is the topic particle, pronounced and learner-romanized wa. Konbanha is an IME key sequence, not the pronunciation guide.

questions.prompt: Which common IME key sequence produces the kana spelling こんばんは?
questions.explanation: The IME must create the written kana は, so its direct key sequence ends in ha even though the particle is pronounced wa.

questions.prompt: In 日本へいきます, how should the direction particle へ be learner-romanized?
questions.explanation: The direction particle is written へ but pronounced and romanized e. Typing he remains the direct way to produce its kana.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly separates the pronunciation and IME input for the object particle を?
questions.explanation: Modern beginner pronunciation and romanization use o, while the IME sequence wo creates the distinct kana を.

questions.prompt: Why is gakkou typed with two k characters when entering がっこう?

options.label: The doubled consonant creates small っ before こ.
The doubled consonant creates the long o sound.
The doubled consonant marks a topic particle.

questions.explanation: A doubled following consonant is a common IME shortcut for small っ. The final ou separately represents the long o sequence こう.

questions.prompt: Which pair can commonly produce the same hiragana し in an IME?
questions.explanation: Shi is the learner-facing Hepburn form, while many IMEs also accept the systematic alias si for し.
